page: Amazon Web Services c6a.large is an AMD-based compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It features a single physical AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz with 2 dedicated vCPUs across 2 threads per core. The host provides 4.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, representing a standard 1:2 ratio of vCPU to memory, and contains no local NVMe or SSD storage. The CPU includes 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 4 MB L3 cache allocations alongside cryptographic and vector hardware features like AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and AVX. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-core execution capability, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 2985.49, placing the instance in the top 25% of evaluated servers. However, due to its low hardware resource count of 2 vCPUs, multi-core and parallel execution benchmarks show lower relative output. Stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores rank in the bottom 25% or lower. Memory bandwidth metrics recorded 30.34 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 21.1 GB/sec for large-block writes, positioning memory system throughput in the lower quartiles.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the c6a.large highlights high per-core execution speeds in small-footprint environments. Because memory bandwidth and overall core count are limited, it provides high execution speed for non-parallel tasks without incurring costs for unneeded system memory or storage capacity. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, single-threaded text processing, basic data compression tasks, and minor single-threaded compilation processes.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 1 physical core delivering 2 vCPUs, 4.0 GB of DDR4 system memory, and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface, it operates without local storage. Hardware support includes AVX, AES, and VAES vector and cryptographic capabilities. Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU execution, achieving top 25% performance in single-threaded stress tests. However, overall multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth remain in lower baseline tiers due to the 2 vCPU resource limit. This instance is suitable for lightweight single-threaded compute workloads, small-scale web serving, and basic text processing where high single-core frequency is required without high memory capacity.
